transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Daniel our Solutions Eng and Sofia from CS. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Ethan Rivers: Yeah Ethan here, CTO.
[00:15] Priya Sharma: Priya, Head of ML.
[00:18] Omar Khalid: Omar, DevOps.
[00:20] Hannah Lee: Hannah, PM.
[00:23] Maya Chen: Awesome. Goal for today is kickoff — line up security/networking, confirm pilot success criteria and next steps for benchmarks and pricing. We'll keep this fairly structured.
[00:34] Daniel Park: Hey — quick note, I'll be focusing on latency tuning options, KV cache patterns, and how we run the initial load tests. There might be a couple of slides I share after the intro.
[00:45] Priya Sharma: Sounds good. Our main concerns: data residency, encryption at rest, and keeping token costs under control. We run a high-volume parsing pipeline so costs matter.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Totally — Redwood can help with cost levers: batching, quantization recommendations, and dedicated capacity to control throughput pricing. We'll map those to your flows.
[01:10] Ethan Rivers: Quick background: we currently use an internal transformer service for entity extraction but spikes in latency during peak shipments. We want better 95th pctl latency and also safer fallbacks — at minimum hosted, but concerned about PII.
[01:28] Maya Chen: Understood. On PII and compliance we can go Dedicated or Private so data doesn't traverse multi-tenant stores; we also support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key control.
[01:40] Omar Khalid: For Private we need to know the Control plane model — we have strict egress rules and an internal audit team. Can Redwood run in our VPC or on-prem?
[01:52] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, Redwood Private can be deployed into a customer VPC or on-prem package for air-gapped environments. There are a couple of patterns — we usually do a Private control plane with service nodes in the customer's network. We'll need your network diagram and KMS details.
[02:08] Omar Khalid: Ok I'll get that. We'll also need SSO/SAML setup for RBAC.
[02:13] Maya Chen: We support SSO via SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning. We'll share a runbook.
[02:20] Hannah Lee: On success criteria for the pilot: improve 95th pctl latency for the entity extraction flow to <250ms, keep token costs under $0.0008 per token equivalent, and maintain zero customer data retention beyond 7 days. Is that doable?
[02:35] Daniel Park: The 250ms 95th is tight but feasible if you use shorter context lengths and a low-latency model variant, plus KV cache warmups for repeated prefixes. For volume bursts, Dedicated with reserved GPUs reduces jitter.
[02:50] Priya Sharma: We also use long context in a small subset — like 2% of requests. How does that affect batching/latency?
[02:58] Daniel Park: Long context hurts batching because it increases compute per request; we can route long-context requests to a larger model shard or a different variant with higher SLO but also run them asynchronously. Part of the pilot is categorizing request types.
[03:15] Ethan Rivers: Can you quantify cost difference between Hosted and Dedicated for our volumes?
[03:20] Maya Chen: We'll model that — I will send a Dedicated sizing + pricing spreadsheet. Typically Dedicated has a monthly commit but much lower per-token unit economics at scale. I'll include burst costs and autoscaling policy templates.
[03:31] Priya Sharma: Security documentation — SOC2 and encryption?
[03:33] Sofia Alvarez: We maintain SOC2, ISO readiness artifacts; for Private we support KMS/HSM integration and customer-managed keys. We'll attach the SOC2 summary and encryption architecture doc to the shared folder.
[03:45] Omar Khalid: Great. On networking, we need details on VPC peering, NAT, egress IPs, and firewall rules. Also, are there persistent IPs for Dedicated nodes?
[03:57] Daniel Park: For Dedicated and Private we can provide predictable egress IP ranges and a VPC peering checklist. For Hosted there are shared IP ranges, so that's less ideal for strict firewall rules.
[04:10] Hannah Lee: What's your recommended pilot scope? A small subset of traffic or synthetic benchmarks?
[04:15] Maya Chen: Two parallel tracks: 1) Synthetic benchmarks to validate latency/cost and 2) Canary with a subset of real traffic after KV cache warmup. We'll do ramp steps and rollback policies.
[04:27] Priya Sharma: For synthetic, we'll want to re-run our production representative prompts.
[04:32] Daniel Park: Please send the prompt set — Daniel will instrument the bench harness. I recommend we include cold-start and hot-warm KV cache scenarios.
[04:42] Ethan Rivers: What about model variants and quantization? We've seen quality regressions before when quantizing too aggressively.
[04:48] Daniel Park: We will recommend quantization profiles per workload. Redwood Optimize can make recommendations and we connect quality monitoring to prompt evals so we catch regressions. We'll set regression thresholds.
[05:02] Maya Chen: Quick administrative: I'll upload the kickoff deck and the Dedicated sizing template after this call. Link: https://redwood.app/slides/cedar-isle-kickoff (note: internal link).
[05:12] Omar Khalid: I'll drop the VPC diagram in the shared drive: s3://cedarisle-infra/redwood-kickoff.
[05:18] Hannah Lee: Can you outline the timeline for the pilot?
[05:22] Maya Chen: Target: start bench tests (synthetic) by 8/20, finish bench by 8/24, pilot canary run 8/26–9/02, review 9/03. We'll adjust based on your availability.
[05:33] Priya Sharma: Sounds reasonable. Who's doing the bench work on Redwood side?
[05:36] Daniel Park: Daniel will lead the bench; Maya will coordinate access and pricing; Sofia will manage onboarding and runbooks.
[05:43] Ethan Rivers: A couple of nitty details — data retention: we need deletion at 7 days or less, and audit logs for every request.
[05:50] Sofia Alvarez: We can set data retention policies and provide audit logs. For Private, logs can be shipped to your SIEM.
[05:58] Omar Khalid: KMS: we want customer-managed keys in AWS KMS with key rotation signals. Any blockers?
[06:05] Daniel Park: No blockers; send the KMS key ARN and we'll configure envelope encryption. If you need HSM-level attestation we'll bring the security team in.
[06:15] Priya Sharma: One more item: are there throttles per route and token-rate limiting we can set?
[06:20] Maya Chen: Yes, per-route throttles, quotas, and alerting in Redwood Console. We'll share recommended rate limits based on your bench results.
[06:29] Hannah Lee: Ok let's hand over to the SE for some technical clarifying questions.
[06:33] Daniel Park: Thanks. Two quick clarifiers: what is your 50th and 95th pctl today for the key extraction flow? And what's the average sequence length?
[06:41] Priya Sharma: 50th is around 120ms, 95th ~520ms on peak; average sequence length is about 180 tokens, spike to 900 on long-context cases.
[06:52] Daniel Park: That's helpful. For the 95th we can aim to bring it down by using lower-latency models for the 98% short flow and route long context to a separate async path. Also we can configure KV cache for common prefixes to drop pctl.
[07:07] Ethan Rivers: For KV cache — does Redwood persist that cache between restarts and is it multi-tenant safe?
[07:13] Daniel Park: Yes, KV is persisted with sharded stores for performance; for Dedicated/Private it's isolated per customer. On Hosted we have tenant isolation logic but if you need strict separation we recommend Dedicated.
[07:28] Omar Khalid: What about rollout strategies? Canary, A/B?
[07:31] Maya Chen: We support canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and automatic fallback to a stable model variant on error thresholds. You can define percent ramps and automatic rollback if latency or error exceeds thresholds.
[07:45] Priya Sharma: Any guidance on prompt engineering to reduce tokens?
[07:49] Daniel Park: Yes, a couple of patterns — structured output, constraints, and token compression. We'll include a short prompt guide and examples tailored to entity extraction.
[07:58] Hannah Lee: Ok, last section: who needs to be in the follow-up latency deep-dive?
[08:02] Maya Chen: Daniel + our infra SRE, Omar and Priya from Cedar Isle, and optionally your audit/security rep. We'll propose times for the week of 8/24.
[08:13] Ethan Rivers: Fine. Anything else?
[08:16] Maya Chen: Quick recap — action items: Maya sends pricing and sizing, Daniel prepares bench plan, Omar provides infra/KMS, Priya provides datasets and SLOs. We'll target bench start 8/20. Thanks everyone.
[08:33] Hannah Lee: Thanks all.
[08:35] Priya Sharma: Thanks.
[08:37] Ethan Rivers: Bye.
[08:38] Maya Chen: Bye — follow-up email with links and dates coming shortly.
[08:45] [end of recording]

Notes on transcript: occasional words were unclear — Fireflies labeled some short segments as Speaker 2 where attribution was ambiguous. There are a few mis-heard tokens (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', 'V-B-C' instead of 'VPC') which we've left as-is to preserve transcription fidelity.
